originalTitle: 'AI or bust:' Tech trade powered stocks through volatile September
summary: Wall Street fared better than expected in September, given the month's historical reputation as the worst month for stocks.
content:
Wall Street fared better than expected in September, given the month's historical reputation as the worst month for stocks. It largely comes down to, you guessed it, the artificial intelligence trade.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) declined by 0.4% for the month as Treasury yields surged. It's down 1.9% from its record high set in August. September has historically been the weakest month for the S&P 500 , with an average decline of 0.6% since 1950.

The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) gained 1.8% after hitting a new peak on Sept. 22. Tech giants Meta ( META ) and AMD ( AMD ), along with a handful of other semiconductor stocks, drove that performance .

Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell by about 4.3%, while the small-cap-focused Russell 2000 ( ^RUT ) dropped by 5.4%.

"It's AI or bust," Interactive Brokers chief strategist Steve Sosnick said, pointing to the divergence in stock performance for the major market indexes.

He added that, although the Nasdaq and S&P 500 outperformed on a relative basis, "if you look under the surface, … there's a lot not to like."

Market conditions tightened in September as Treasury yields surged to multi-decade highs. The 2-year and 10-year ( ^TNX ) yields each rose by roughly half a percentage point, and the 30-year ( ^TYX ) yield climbed nearly 40 basis points since the end of August.

The last time all three government bonds moved that much was September 2022 , during the Fed's last hiking cycle.

Read more:  How soaring Treasury yields could hit your finances

The pressure on equities has also shown up in the IPO market. Smart-ring maker Oura postponed its planned offering this week , joining companies like Holtec Nuclear and Bamboo Insurance in citing uncertain market conditions as reasons to pull back on their debuts.

Frontier AI company Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) has also reportedly pushed back its planned public debut from October to November. The listing was already expected to be the marquee IPO of the fourth quarter. It now represents an even clearer test of how far investor enthusiasm for AI can stretch .

Yet investors have largely powered through those pressures under the premise that the AI boom cannot be stopped.

UBS chief economist Arend Kapteyn said Wednesday that AI-related investment, along with the wealth effect created by rising AI stocks, now accounts for 80% or more of US economic growth.

"It just looks like AI is neutralizing everything, at least on an aggregate level," Kapteyn said. UBS recently lifted its estimate for AI-driven capital spending next year by $200 billion to $1.4 trillion. Non-AI component investment, by contrast, is "running at zero," Kapteyn added.

Read more:  How to protect your portfolio from an AI bubble

The economic concentration is just the latest reminder of the mounting risks if the AI trade topples. Kapteyn said the wealth created by rising AI stocks has helped support consumer spending, particularly among higher-income households.

A sudden reversal could therefore hit the economy twice — through slowing business investment and weakening consumption.

So far, however, UBS sees signs that the boom is beginning to spread beyond the technology sector. Kapteyn said every dollar of AI-related capital spending this quarter appears to generate roughly $1.50 of investment in the following quarter, with only about a third of that follow-on spending going toward technology.

David Hollerith covers a range of developments throughout the financial sector, from Wall Street to banking and asset management to crypto and fintech. Email him at david.hollerith@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on X at @DsHollers.

chineseTitle: “AI 或破产：”科技交易推动股市度过动荡的九月
chineseSummary: 鉴于该月历史上被誉为股市表现最差的月份，华尔街 9 月份的表现好于预期。
chineseContent:
鉴于该月历史上被誉为股市表现最差的月份，华尔街 9 月份的表现好于预期。你猜对了，这很大程度上归结于人工智能行业。

由于美国国债收益率飙升，标准普尔 500 指数 (^GSPC) 本月下跌 0.4%。较 8 月份创下的历史高位下跌 1.9%。 9 月历来是标准普尔 500 指数最弱的月份，自 1950 年以来平均下跌 0.6%。

纳斯达克综合指数 (^IXIC) 在 9 月 22 日创下新高后上涨 1.8%。科技巨头 Meta (META) 和 AMD (AMD) 以及其他一些半导体股票推动了这一表现。

与此同时，道琼斯工业平均指数 (^DJI) 下跌约 4.3%，而以小盘股为主的罗素 2000 指数 (^RUT) 下跌 5.4%。

盈透证券首席策略师史蒂夫·索斯尼克表示：“要么人工智能，要么破产。”他指出主要市场指数的股票表现存在差异。

他补充说，尽管纳斯达克指数和标准普尔 500 指数相对表现优于大盘，但“如果你深入观察，……有很多不喜欢的地方。”

随着美国国债收益率飙升至数十年来的高点，市场状况在 9 月份收紧。自8月底以来，2年期和10年期（^TNX）收益率分别上涨了约半个百分点，30年期（^TYX）收益率攀升了近40个基点。

上一次这三种政府债券变动幅度如此之大是在 2022 年 9 月，即美联储上一次加息周期期间。

阅读更多内容：国债收益率飙升如何影响您的财务状况

股市面临的压力也体现在IPO市场上。智能环制造商 Oura 推迟了本周的上市计划，加入 Holtec Nuclear 和 Bamboo Insurance 等公司的行列，以不确定的市场状况为理由推迟上市。

据报道，Frontier AI 公司 Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) 也将其计划从 10 月公开亮相推迟到 11 月。预计此次上市将成为第四季度最引人注目的首次公开募股(IPO)。现在，它是对投资者对人工智能的热情能延伸到何种程度的更清晰的考验。

然而，在人工智能热潮无法阻止的前提下，投资者很大程度上顶住了这些压力。

瑞银首席经济学家 Arend Kapteyn 周三表示，人工智能相关投资，加上人工智能股票上涨所创造的财富效应，目前对美国经济增长的贡献率达到 80% 或更多。

卡普坦说：“看起来人工智能正在中和一切，至少在总体水平上是这样。”瑞银最近将明年人工智能驱动的资本支出预期上调了 2000 亿美元，达到 1.4 万亿美元。相比之下，非人工智能组件投资“为零”，Kapteyn 补充道。

了解更多：如何保护您的投资组合免受人工智能泡沫的影响

经济集中化只是最新一次提醒人们，如果人工智能贸易崩溃，风险将不断增加。卡普坦表示，人工智能股票上涨所创造的财富有助于支持消费者支出，特别是高收入家庭的支出。

因此，突然的逆转可能会对经济造成双重打击——商业投资放缓和消费疲软。

然而，到目前为止，瑞银看到有迹象表明，繁荣开始蔓延到科技行业之外。 Kapteyn 表示，本季度每 1 美元的人工智能相关资本支出似乎都会在下个季度产生约 1.5 美元的投资，其中只有约三分之一的后续支出用于技术。
